title: A wider transiting planet
hook: Change planet radius and predict ideal fractional transit depth.
misconception: ideal fractional transit depth doubles when planet radius doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply depth ≈ (R_planet/R_star)² to compare ideal fractional transit depth when planet radius changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a small opaque planet crossing a uniform stellar disk of fixed radius without limb darkening, depth ≈ (R_planet/R_star)². When planet radius doubles, ideal fractional transit depth becomes 4 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model depth ≈ (R_planet/R_star)²; scaling exponent 2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a small opaque planet crossing a uniform stellar disk of fixed radius without limb darkening, with a nonzero initial result. If planet radius triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on ideal fractional transit depth?
recall.why: Apply depth ≈ (R_planet/R_star)² under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 9.
